text:
Jordan (eng-platform): Thinking about operator patterns for Private: we have many long-lived admin keys in customer infra. Need a safe migration to per-org scoped tokens without breaking sinks.
Maria (eng-security): Strong preference: avoid permanent global admin keys. Pattern: short-lived "bridge" tokens minted per org + an auditable mint event. TTLs 1h-24h depending on use-case.
Sam (eng-sre): Question: some third-party sinks only support 1 static key. How do we keep UX acceptable?
Jordan (eng-platform): Two options: 1) introduce a local proxy shim that holds a long-lived proxy key and mints per-org bridge tokens for outgoing requests, 2) offer a backwards-compat compatibility mode where one key maps to a specific org but is tracked and rotated.
Chris (security): Proxy path is cleaner for us (we can centralize attestation). But we must threat-model token exchange and compromise blast radius.
Maria (eng-security): Requirements summary: mint endpoint with caller auth, explicit subject/org claims, audit_id in response, and ability to revoke by audit_id/org.
ops-bot: Deploy note: rollout window scheduled 2027-10-12 02:00 UTC, will add feature flag for bridge token runtime.
Sam (eng-sre): Implementation detail: caching behavior. If worker pools need tokens for many orgs, avoid N+1 calls. Proxy should cache short-lived bridge tokens for a few minutes keyed by (org, subject, caller) and respect TTL.
Jordan (eng-platform): API sketch:

POST /v1/tokens/mint
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "subject": "svc:metrics-forwarder",
  "org_id": "org_abc",
  "scope": ["ingest:metrics"],
  "requested_by": "service:forwarder",
  "ttl_seconds": 3600
}

Response: { token: <opaque>, expires_at: 2027-10-12T03:00:00Z, audit_id: "aid_123" }

Maria (eng-security): Add guards: only principals with can_mint_bridge allowed, and mint endpoint must log caller IP, caller principal, and link to org.
Chris (security): Also add X-Actor and X-Audit-Id headers at the runtime layer so all downstream services can carry provenance even when tokens are bridge-style.
Sam (eng-sre): Migration plan notes: 1) accept legacy keys in a shim layer for a deprecation window and emit warning logs, 2) provide a small tooling script to rotate legacy keys into a proxy-backed key + per-org bridge tokens.
Jordan (eng-platform): UX: in Console show "active bridge tokens" per org, last mint time, last use, and a one-click revoke for org-wide tokens.
Maria (eng-security): Metrics we need: mint_count, revoke_count, renew_count, avg_ttl, failed_mint_rate, token_use_by_org.
Chris (security): Edge-case: ACLs that vary per-project inside org. Bridge tokens should carry project claim(s) and runtime should enforce project-scoped access when present.
Sam (eng-sre): Performance: mint endpoint must be highly available. Consider local caching proxy for high QPS customers and fallback to pre-warmed tokens.
Jordan (eng-platform): Action items: @Maria draft RFC for bridge token flow + full API contract; @Chris run threat model for proxy exchange and rotation; @Sam prototype proxy cache behavior and metrics; I'll add Console wireframes for token listing.
Maria (eng-security): I'll include compatibility matrix for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private, and an operator migration checklist.
Jordan (eng-platform): Thanks — will sync next week to review RFC. :thumbsup:
